Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create two Verilog modules: one for the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) block and one for the Inverse Discrete Cosine Transform (IDCT) block. 
The DCT and IDCT blocks are widely used in signal processing applications such as image and audio compression. 

The DCT block takes a sequence of n input samples and produces a sequence of n frequency coefficients. 
The IDCT block takes a sequence of n frequency coefficients and produces a sequence of n output samples. 
The DCT and IDCT blocks are closely related, and are often used together in applications such as JPEG image compression.

Your DCT module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: a set of n input samples (in1, in2, ..., inn)
Outputs: a set of n frequency coefficients (out1, out2, ..., outn)

Your IDCT module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: a set of n frequency coefficients (in1, in2, ..., inn)
Outputs: a set of n output samples (out1, out2, ..., outn)

You should implement the DCT and IDCT blocks using the mathematical formulas for the transforms. 
The formulas are given below:

DCT:
out[k] = 2*sum(i=0 to n-1)[in[i]*cos(pi*k*(2*i+1)/(2*n))] for k=0 to n-1

IDCT:
out[i] = 2/n * sum(k=0 to n-1)[out[k]*cos(pi*k*(2*i+1)/(2*n))] for i=0 to n-1

To implement the DCT and IDCT blocks, you should use Verilog code to define the mathematical formulas as functions of the input samples and frequency coefficients. 
You should then use these functions to connect the inputs to the outputs.
